sections.summary: Thailand legislates severance payments based on years of service.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Thailand legislates severance payments based on years of service.

sections.label: DBS financial wellness Gen Z Millennials
sections.summary: DBS's 2025 financial wellness series found Gen Zs and Millennials aged 25 to 44 face heavier liabilities and lag in retirement savings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: According to DBS Bank's 2025 instalment of its financial wellness series, which analysed aggregated and anonymised data from approximately two million DBS and POSB retail customers, Gen Zs and Millennials aged 25 to 44 are increasingly shouldering heavier liabilities and are falling behind their older counterparts in building retirement savings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Among pre-retirement age groups, those aged 35 to 44 are the most financially stretched, with debts slightly overweighing liquid assets, largely due to housing vehicle and credit card loans.

sections.label: Employers' Federation Employment Act review caution
sections.summary: The Singapore National Employers' Federation cautioned that the Employment Act review should not inadvertently mandate practices reducing employer flexibilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In fact, when the Government announced the review of the Employment Act last year, the Singapore National Employers' Federation cautioned that the review should not, and I quote, "inadvertently mandate progressive employment practices that may reduce flexibilities for employers and undermine business competitiveness".

sections.label: Collective agreements retrenchment benefit benchmarks
sections.summary: Collective agreements already prescribe retrenchment benefits, and most employers converge at those benchmarks, few paying above the one-month norm.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, the facts do not fully support this concern.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: There are already collective agreements that prescribe retrenchment benefits and the vast majority of employers converge at those benchmarks anyway, with a very small number paying more than the one-month norm for each year of service.

sections.label: Employers providing retrenchment benefits
sections.summary: Eight out of 10 eligible employees already receive retrenchment benefits up to the tripartite guideline of two weeks salary per year of service.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Those concerns deserve attention and respect, because it is neither simple nor straightforward to start, build or sustain a business.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, we should not forget that many responsible employers already provide retrenchment benefits: eight out of 10 eligible employees already receive retrenchment benefits up to the tripartite guideline of two weeks salary for every year of service.

sections.label: Subsidiary legislation for higher payouts
sections.summary: Subsidiary legislation could direct higher retrenchment payouts for larger firms, up to one month's salary per year of service.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: A statutory framework could also be enhanced by subsidiary legislation directing higher payouts for larger firms, such as up to the union norm of one month salary for every year of service, something which larger global MNCs in particular would not necessarily baulk at, especially since they are already subject to legislative regimes governing retrenchment benefits in other countries where they operate.

sections.label: Retrenchment benefit approaches abroad
sections.summary: Other countries use national insurance schemes, wage guarantee agreements, or treat retrenchment benefits as preferential debt in insolvency.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Some create backstops, such as national insurance schemes, while others advance wage guarantee agreements, while yet others treat retrenchment benefits as a preferential debt through insolvency laws.

sections.label: Statutory retrenchment benefits framework urged
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Government to convene employers, unions and workers to develop a statutory retrenchment benefits framework with legislation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Trust and commitment to an employer is strengthened when workers know that after years of service, if restructuring occurs through no fault of their own, they will receive fair and meaningful protection.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Therefore, as part of the Government's implementation of the ESR, I urge the Government to convene employers, unions and workers to develop a statutory retrenchment benefits framework with the objective of introducing legislation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: A resilient society requires workers who know they will not be left to bear the burdens of economic change alone, because in line with the call of the Labour Movement in NTUC, no less, while not every job can be protected, every worker deserves protection.

sections.label: Good jobs and incomes strategy
sections.summary: In Singapore, good jobs and incomes are the main channel through which economic growth benefits Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In Singapore, the main channel through which economic growth benefits Singaporeans is good jobs and incomes.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This remains the central socio-economic strategy, as affirmed in the recent debate in this House on an AI transition with no jobless growth.

sections.label: Adult skills literacy and numeracy
sections.summary: Singapore tops test scores of 15-year-olds but ranks mid-pack among OECD economies in adult literacy and numeracy.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Singapore tops the world in test scores of 15-year-olds, but can we top the world in the skills and learning agility of 45-year-olds?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development's (OECD's) survey of adult skills suggest that we are only in the middle of the pack relative to OECD economies in adult literacy and numeracy.

sections.label: Skills-first hiring and learning roles
sections.summary: Leaders, HR professionals, line managers and unions enable learning, and organisations should adopt skills-first practices for hiring and advancement.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Leaders, human resource (HR) professionals, line managers and unions all have a role to play in enabling learning by activating mindsets, securing training resources, embedding learning and work, and creating conducive environments for learning and experimentation.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It should also be a priority for organisations to adopt skills-first practices, where skills, rather than credentials, become the key consideration for hiring, career development and advancement.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This will give employers access to a larger pool of talent, while workers will enjoy greater career mobility as they are not limited by their previous educational qualifications or work experience, but can leverage the skills they have picked up through work to take on new job roles or cross into other sectors.

sections.label: Institute of Adult Learning framework
sections.summary: The Institute of Adult Learning will launch a skills-first framework for action in October setting out actions and behaviours for individuals, employers and training providers.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Institute of Adult Learning will be launching a skills-first framework for action in October, which will set out concrete actions and behaviours that we hope will become widely adopted by individuals, employers and training providers.

sections.label: Skills credentialing for sectors
sections.summary: The Institute of Adult Learning has pioneered skills credentialing for the training and adult education sector and is working with partner agencies to adapt it for other sectors.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Institute of Adult Learning has pioneered skills credentialing for the training and adult education sector, and we are working with partner agencies to adapt this methodology for other sectors.

sections.label: Supporting enterprises as learning organisations
sections.summary: There is a need to support enterprises in becoming learning organisations through practical tool kits and resources, helping leaders and HR place learning at the heart of strategy.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Third, there is a need to support enterprises in becoming learning organisations by providing practical tool kits and resources to strengthen organisational capabilities, while helping leaders, HR and organisational development professionals place learning at the heart of organisational strategy and unlock the potential of their workforce.

sections.label: Support for micro entrepreneurship ventures
sections.summary: The Government could review what more could be done to support such ventures through financing, AI compute access, business networks, mentoring or other targeted support.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Government could review what more could be done to support such ventures, whether through financing, access to AI compute, business networks and mentoring, or other targeted forms of support to encourage micro entrepreneurship as a viable career pathway or source of supplementary income for Singaporeans.

sections.label: Matching ambition with investment
sections.summary: The passage calls for matching ambition for the workforce with sustained investment in expertise and capability.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Let us match our ambition for our workforce with sustained investment in expertise and capability.

sections.label: ESR committee representation concerns
sections.summary: The ESR mainly comprises C-suite and NTUC union leaders, and organisations representing migrant workers, women's rights and persons with disabilities should have been more clearly represented.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Of the members and five committees involved in the ESR, it appears to mainly comprise C-suite and the NTUC union leaders.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Even as we recognise their insights, organisations representing migrant workers, women's rights and persons with disabilities should also have been more clearly represented.

sections.label: Median wages of care workers
sections.summary: MOM data as of June 2025 shows median gross monthly wages of $5,129 for registered nurses, $4,565 for social workers and $4,150 for preschool teachers.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Latest MOM data as of June 2025 indicates the median gross wage earned by registered nurses at $5,129 per month.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Social workers earn $4,565, preschool teachers earn $4,150.

sections.label: Burnout study in public healthcare
sections.summary: A 2022 study in the Academy of Medicine journal found high emotional exhaustion in 37.8%, high de-personalisation in 29.7% and low personal accomplishment in 55.3% of respondents.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: A 2022 study published in the Academy of Medicine, Singapore's official journal measuring burnout in the public healthcare sector between July 2019 and January 2020 found that 37.8% of respondents had high emotional exhaustion scores; 29.7% had high de-personalisation scores and 55.3% had low personal accomplishment scores.

sections.label: Care economy investment and informal caregiving
sections.summary: The passage asks how to support more startups in the care economy, urges raiSE SG to review the ecosystem with MTI and MSF, and cites a study valuing informal senior caregiving at $1.28 billion yearly.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: While the current existence of the VentureForGood Grant administered by raiSE SG supports early and growth-stage social enterprises for up to $300,000 in capital expenditure and operating costs, how can we support more startups and commercial enterprises in this space to bring sustainable investments into the care economy? raiSE SG must work with the Ministry of Trade and Industry, and the Ministry of Social and Family Development jointly to review the care economy investment ecosystem to build a more sustainable investment and employment ecosystem.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Caregiving is also borne by informal carers, such as family and friends.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This labour of love is not reflected in GDP figures, but its importance is underscored by the inaugural Duke-National University of Singapore study, which valued the economic contribution of informal caregiving for seniors at $1.28 billion annually.

sections.label: SME growth stage capital access
sections.summary: The ESR report acknowledges companies find it difficult to secure growth stage capital and that Temasek participates in SME co-investment, while businesses need broader access to financing.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: For SME looking to scale, the ESR report acknowledges that companies still find it difficult to secure growth stage capital and that Temasek already participates in SME co-investment.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: But what our businesses need to grow is bolder and broader base access to financing catalysed by private and public capital.

sections.label: Ecosystem protecting entrepreneurial risk-taking
sections.summary: The passage states that encouraging would-be entrepreneurs requires an ecosystem with structural measures to protect necessary risk-taking for success.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: To further encourage would-be entrepreneurs, we also need an ecosystem with structural measures to protect necessary risk-taking for success.

sections.label: EU second chance policy for entrepreneurs
sections.summary: A 2011 EU expert group report said second chance policy for bankrupt entrepreneurs may be a promising policy option, and the EU has since adopted a preventive restructuring approach.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: A European Union (EU) expert group report in 2011 that, "A second chance policy that enables formally bankrupt entrepreneurs to restart may represent one of the most promising and under-exploited policy options for company creation and job growth." The EU has since adopted a more balanced preventive restructuring approach for bona fide entrepreneurs seeking a second chance.

sections.label: Data centres moved to Johor, Batam
sections.summary: The 2019 data centre moratorium and higher operating costs drove operators to Johor and Batam, with Singaporean companies owning the largest capacity share there.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The earlier 2019 moratorium on new data centres, as well as higher operating costs here, drove operators to set up shop in neighbouring Johor and Batam, with Singaporean companies owning the largest proportion of data centre capacity in both regions.

sections.label: Forest clearing and rising consumption
sections.summary: Concern mounts over forests cleared for housing and development, while EMA reported 4% higher electricity use in 2024 and PUB expects non-domestic water use to reach 60% by 2065.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Concern is mounting over forests being cut down for housing, both at Maju Forest and Gillman Barracks, alongside a patch of forest near Woodlands Checkpoint, which would be cleared for the development of a new commercial hub, while over 52 hectares of forested land would be cut down for the next phase of the Jurong Innovation District.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: EMA noted that electricity consumption increased by 4% year-on-year in 2024, with commerce and service-related businesses consuming the highest proportion that year at 40.2% of our total electricity use.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Already, non-domestic water consumption takes up 55% of our total water use and PUB estimates that this is expected to increase to 60% by 2065.

sections.label: AI disrupting jobs
sections.summary: AI will disrupt jobs at a speed and scale not seen before.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: AI will disrupt jobs at a speed and scale that we have not seen before.

sections.label: Retrenchment benefits and unemployment support
sections.summary: Two topics are retrenchment benefits and unemployment support, and NTUC and tripartite partners work to ensure no worker is left behind.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: There are two topics in this space, firstly, on retrenchment benefits and unemployment support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: And on the topic of mandating retrenchment benefits, the NTUC and the Labour Movement, including myself, have been working with tripartite partners to ensure that no worker is left behind.

sections.label: Lobbying to strengthen retrenchment protection
sections.summary: The speaker has lobbied for a decade to strengthen retrenchment protection, and tripartite partners remain open in negotiations on the Employment Act and advisories.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: In fact, we have been trying to lobby, myself inclusive, in this House, for the past decade, including earlier this year, for further strengthening of the retrenchment protection regime here in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: In fact, the tripartite partners, as I am involved in the negotiations for the Employment Act as well as all the relevant statutory provisions as well as advisories, we remain open in negotiating and discussions are underway, whether it is the Employment Act reviewing the Tripartite Advisory to strengthen it to tripartite guidelines, which I have raised before in this House, and even stronger measures against companies that flopped or failed to, comply with advisories.

sections.label: Unemployment insurance support introduced
sections.summary: The speaker lobbied over a decade for unemployment support, and the SkillsFuture Jobseeker Support Scheme was implemented on 26 April last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: On the topic of unemployment insurance support, this is something I spoke about more than a decade ago, lobbying for some form of unemployment support for workers in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: I am very happy that it has been introduced last year, on 26 April – I remember the fateful date – the SkillsFuture Jobseeker Support Scheme was implemented.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Jobseeker Support income threshold
sections.summary: Speaker says the SkillsFuture Jobseeker Support scheme's $5,000 income threshold could be reviewed and raised to the median salary of PMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: And I have, at the same time, in this same House, also lobbied for this area to be further expanded and rebuilt, now that we are seeing in the last 24 months more PMEs being affected by lay-offs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: So, that is an area which we can review, whether the income threshold of the SkillsFuture Jobseeker Support scheme can be raised – because currently, that is $5,000 – whether it can be raised to the median salary of PMEs, so, that is one avenue to explore.

sections.label: Tripartite Jobs Council formation
sections.summary: MOM, NTUC and the Singapore National Employers Federation announced the Tripartite Jobs Council, initiated by NTUC, to coordinate programmes helping workers reskill and businesses redesign jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)

sections.label: Amended Motion's economic combination
sections.summary: The amended Motion captures an equal and inclusive economy with opportunities, and an economy powered by local companies, global enterprises, demand and Singaporeans venturing abroad.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Energy and Industry) (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The amended Motion, Mr Speaker, captures the full combination that Singapore needs: an equal and inclusive economy with opportunities for entrepreneurs, households, businesses and workers, and ideas and innovation to flourish; and an economy powered by dynamic local companies and global enterprises, healthy domestic and external demand, and Singaporeans and Singaporean capital venturing abroad.

sections.label: Government's role in economy
sections.summary: The Government will maintain a trusted, open economy, invest long term, address capability, financing and market-access gaps, and help workers prepare for change.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Energy and Industry) (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The Government will play its part: maintaining a trusted, open economy; investing for the long term; addressing genuine capability, financing and market-access gaps; and helping workers prepare for change.

sections.label: Fair chance and support
sections.summary: The passage states that timing and opportunity are for entrepreneurs to decide, while Singapore can ensure fair chances, pathways and support.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Energy and Industry) (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Because we cannot provide the timing and the opportunity, that is the most crucial part that the entrepreneur and the business founder would have to decide.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Energy and Industry) (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: But what we can always do is to ensure that Singapore remains a place where every person has a fair chance to try, a pathway to progress and the support to recover from setbacks.

sections.label: MTI renaming and enterprise support
sections.summary: MTI will be renamed Ministry of Energy, Trade and Industry from 1 October 2026, with support for Singaporean enterprises anchoring here.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Minister Dr Tan, would you like to respond?

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We certainly will do our best to support all of our Singapore homegrown enterprise.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: In fact, if you look at the renaming and the most recent Cabinet reshuffling, the Ministry of Trade and Industry will be renamed as Ministry of Energy, Trade and Industry with effect from 1 October 2026.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Our Prime Minister is enlightened, he has seen how potentially all of the disruptions, the expanse of the opportunities that are available.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: And therefore, given the size and the scope of what we all have to do, Deputy Prime Minister Gan in his experience, overseeing trade and the macroeconomic strategy; and I will look at energy and industry, and I will actively engage the trade associations and chambers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We will look to as many expert guidance and also invite possible openings for us to see how we can better support our Singaporean enterprises and our fellow Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: But of course, with one main outcome – and that is they have to anchor themselves here in our beloved homeland.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Speaker, I thank every Member who spoke on both sides of this House.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We filed this Motion to provide answers to the economic worries top-of-mind for every Singaporean: whether there is a job and whether it lasts; whether the young person who has done everything asked of them can find work that goes somewhere; whether a flat is within reach; whether a small shop can survive its rent; whether the course a worker is sent on leads to a job; whether the growth we announced is felt in a wage; whether a Singaporean who wants to build something can afford to do it in spite of the high cost structure here.

sections.label: Special zone around NTU
sections.summary: A special zone around NTU is proposed where state land is charged at development cost rather than market scarcity value.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: First, how do we foster a dynamic innovation ecosystem that can overcome and maximise value in spite of high business cost and physical constraints?

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I proposed a special zone around NTU, where state land is charged at development cost rather than market scarcity value.

sections.label: Tenders, compute and Fair Start
sections.summary: Proposals include concept and price tenders, an HDB model for compute, and a Fair Start Promise for young Singaporeans under 30.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: He proposed concept and price tenders as the default for strategic sites, because a system where the highest bidder wins, the reserve price is unpublished and unawarded sites simply can wait, can only ratchet upward.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And he proposed an "HDB model for compute", because we take some $20 billion a year in land sales and set aside only about $150 million for a one-year compute programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Mr Andre Low proposed a Fair Start Promise, a national commitment to work towards a simple goal that young Singaporeans under 30, making the transition from education or NS into working life will get a fair start through stable employment or a proper paid career-building pathway.

sections.label: Dinesh agrees on fair start
sections.summary: Minister of State Dinesh broadly agreed with Mr Andre Low's proposals and shared the aspiration of a fair start for young Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Minister of State Dinesh broadly agreed with Mr Andre Low's proposals and acknowledged that he shared our aspiration of giving every young Singaporean a fair start.

sections.label: Universal redundancy insurance scheme
sections.summary: Mr Fadli Fawzi proposed a universal redundancy insurance scheme with combined contributions, 40% of last drawn pay, capped and lasting up to six months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Mr Fadli Fawzi proposed a universal redundancy insurance scheme, employer and employee together combining one-tenth of 1% of monthly salary, paying 40% of last drawn pay, capped at 40% of median, up to six months, with no application to make, because a worker who must apply and may be refused cannot plan.

sections.label: Retrenchment benefits statutory floor
sections.summary: He proposed legislating a statutory retrenchment benefits floor now, as courts confirmed section 45 creates no entitlement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As a matter of law, currently, there is nothing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: He proposed legislating a statutory floor for retrenchment benefits at a tripartite norm of two weeks' salary for each year of service.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: He also proposed subsidiary legislation directing higher payouts for larger firms, up to the union norm of a month's salary a year and he proposed doing it now because the Courts have confirmed a gap.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This year, the Employment Claims Tribunals held that section 45 of the Employment Act creates no entitlement, and the tripartite guidelines create no legal basis, for one.

sections.label: Family caregiver compensation proposals
sections.summary: She proposed caregiver compensation, expanded respite care and time use studies, citing $1.28 billion in informal senior caregiving.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: A wage floor was not built currently to reach them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: She proposed compensation for family caregivers, expanded respite care and regular official time use studies, because informal caregiving for seniors was valued at $1.28 billion a year and appears in no national account.

sections.label: Capability before ownership
sections.summary: Capability makes ownership possible; targeting ownership without capability and competitiveness may leave us with a smaller pie.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Capability is what makes ownership possible, rather than the other way around.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: If we make rebalancing the organising principle of our strategy, we may not end up with more of these companies, we may end up with fewer.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Target ownership without capability and competitiveness and we do not own more of the pie, we own more of a smaller one.

sections.label: WP rejects Amendment No 1
sections.summary: On Amendment No 1, to delete "notwithstanding" and insert "in line with", the WP cannot accept this amendment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: On Amendment No 1, to delete "notwithstanding" and insert "in line with", the WP cannot accept this amendment.

sections.label: Fourth national economic blueprint
sections.summary: The ESR is the fourth national economic blueprint since 2010.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The ESR is the fourth national economic blueprint since 2010.

sections.label: Productivity and enterprise goals
sections.summary: The 2% to 3% productivity growth goal was met; the 1,000 local companies goal was not tracked after 2017.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: One on productivity – to "achieve productivity growth of 2% to 3% per year over the next 10 years." This goal was met.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: One on enterprises – "We can raise this number significantly to reach 1,000 such enterprises over the next 10 years." Local companies with revenue over $100 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This goal of 1,000 local companies with revenue over $100 million was not tracked after 2017, when the report recorded about 800 such companies.

sections.label: Manufacturing share and targets
sections.summary: Manufacturing was 17.4% of GDP in 2016 and 2025, and the 2026 ESR repeats a target on billion-dollar Singapore-headquartered companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Manufacturing was 17.4% of GDP in 2016 and remains 17.4% in 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: From the 2021 Emerging Stronger Taskforce, I could find no macroeconomic targets at all.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And in this 2026 ESR, the only target-shaped sentence, appearing twice, reads: "we should set an ambitious target to significantly increase the number of Singapore headquartered companies with more than $1 billion in revenue".

sections.label: 30 by 30 dropped
sections.summary: The food policy 30 by 30 was dropped last November for narrower targets, five years later.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The food policy "30 by 30" was dropped last November for narrower targets, five years later.

sections.label: Three amendments and disagreement
sections.summary: Three of four amendments are accounted for, and no consensus was reached on the amended Motion due to disagreement over the term notwithstanding.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: So, that accounts for three of the four amendments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: We regret that we are not able to achieve consensus on the amended Motion today, that the disagreement has founded on the term "notwithstanding", as opposed to what we are proposing, which is in line with the ESR.

sections.label: Difficult world, stiffer competition
sections.summary: The world is very difficult and external competition has become stiffer.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: Most importantly, we are in a very difficult world, a world where external competition has become stiffer.

sections.label: Retrenchment payout norm and distress
sections.summary: The norm is two weeks to one month salary per year of service, and mandatory payments may weaken firms with cash flow issues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee
sentences.text: The current norm actually ranges between two weeks and one month salary per year of service, but the Member has proposed at least one month for larger companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee
sentences.text: And for those they are facing serious cash flow issues, if such payments are mandatory, would the Member not agree that this push might weaken firms into deeper distress and potentially putting remaining jobs at risk?

sections.label: Security is next good job
sections.summary: The best security for a retrenched worker is not only a payout but the ability to find the next good job.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee
sentences.text: Because ultimately, the best security for a retrenched worker is not only a payout, but the ability to find the next good job.

sections.label: Amendment No 1 question
sections.summary: The House is asked to decide on Amendment No 1, which deletes 'not withstanding' and inserts 'in line with'.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: We have now come to the conclusion of the debate and I shall put forth the questions to the House for a decision.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: We have four amendments proposed by Mr Edward Chia.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Amendment No 1 is, "In line 1, to delete 'not withstanding' and insert 'in line with'." The Question is, “That Amendment No 1 be made”.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Amendment No 2 is, "In line 5, to delete 'economic engine driven' and insert 'economy powered'."

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Amendment No 3, "In line 5, after the words 'local companies', to insert 'global enterprises,'."

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
